in_arabic.name: معاوية
in_arabic.meaning: اسم مشتق من عوى يدل على القوة والشجاعة
in_arabic.long_meaning: معاوية هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي، مشتق من فعل 'عوى' الذي يعني الصراخ أو الدعاء، يدل على القوة والشجاعة، وغالبًا ما يرتبط بالقيادة والحماية. في التاريخ الإسلامي، كان معاوية بن أبي سفيان أحد الخلفاء الأُمويين الأوائل.

in_urdu.name: معاویہ
in_urdu.meaning: ایک ایسا نام جو قوت اور شجاعت کی طرف اشارہ کرتا ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: معاویہ ایک عربی نام ہے جس کا مطلب ہے 'ایک ایسا نام جو قوت اور شجاعت کی طرف اشارہ کرتا ہے'۔ یہ نام عوی سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے 'صراخ کرنا یا پکارنا'۔ تاریخی طور پر، معاویہ بن ابی سفیان خلافت امویہ کے پہلے خلیفہ تھے اور ان کا نام اسلامی تاریخ میں اہم کردار ادا کرنے والوں میں سے ایک ہے۔

in_hindi.name: मुआविया
in_hindi.meaning: एक नाम जो शक्ति और बहादुरी की ओर संकेत करता है
in_hindi.long_meaning: मुआविया एक अरबी नाम है जिसका अर्थ है 'एक नाम जो शक्ति और बहादुरी की ओर संकेत करता है'। यह नाम 'अवी' से लिया गया है, जिसका अर्थ है 'चिल्लाना या पुकारना'। ऐतिहासिक रूप से, मुआविया बिन अबी सुफियान उमय्यद खलीफा थे और उनका नाम इस्लामी इतिहास में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाने वालों में से एक है।

in_english.name: Mu'Awiyyah
in_english.meaning: A name indicating strength and bravery
in_english.long_meaning: Mu'Awiyyah is a masculine given name derived from the Arabic root 'ʿ-w-y' (عوى), meaning 'to cry out or call'. It signifies strength, bravery, and leadership qualities. Historically, Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan was a prominent figure in Islamic history, serving as the first caliph of the Umayyad Caliphate. The name is associated with courage, resilience, and strong leadership skills.

data.cultural_impact: Mu'Awiyyah was the founder of the Umayyad Dynasty, the third Islamic caliphate after the Rashidun Caliphate. He ruled from 661 to 680 CE and is known for extending the Muslim empire by conquering much of the Eastern Roman Empire and North Africa. The Umayyad Empire lasted for over two centuries and became renowned for its artistic, architectural, and cultural achievements.
data.spiritual_significance: Despite his political and military accomplishments, Mu'Awiyyah is also remembered for his devotion to Islam and his close relationship with the Prophet Muhammad. He famously led the funeral prayers for Imam Hasan, the second Shia Imam, and was noted for his piety and rigorous adherence to Islamic law. This aspect of his life is often emphasized in Islamic historical and spiritual discourse, highlighting the balance between political power and spiritual commitment.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Mu'Awiyyah ibn Abi Sufyan (570-680 CE) was the founder of the Umayyad Caliphate in Damascus. The name Mu'Awiyyah carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Mu'Awiyyah was a prominent figure in early Islamic history. He was the governor of Syria under the first caliph, Abu Bakr, and later became the founder of the Umayyad Caliphate in Damascus. His reign marked the end of the Rashidun Caliphate and the beginning of the Umayyad Dynasty.
